title: Tool failures and retries: is_error, backoff, and guardrails

events.label: Pose the task
events.detail: "Sync yesterday's refund orders into the reconciliation system and produce a summary." — two tool calls: query first, then write.

events.label: tool_use #1: wrong parameter
events.detail: {"id":"toolu_r1","name":"query_refunds","input":{"date":"09/07"}} — date expects ISO format (2026-09-07), the model wrote 09/07. Bad parameters are among the most common failures.

events.label: Validation rejects it
events.detail: Local schema validation fails: date does not match the YYYY-MM-DD format. The request never reached the ledger system — the validator's job is to stop bad parameters before execution.

events.label: Feed back verbatim with is_error=true
events.detail: {"type":"tool_result","tool_use_id":"toolu_r1","is_error":true,"content":"invalid date format: expected YYYY-MM-DD, got 09/07"}. Two things matter: is_error tells the model it failed rather than returning an empty result, and the error text goes back verbatim so the model knows how to fix it.

events.label: Retry with corrected parameters as tool_use #2
events.detail: New request {"id":"toolu_r2","name":"query_refunds","input":{"date":"2026-09-07"}} — the model read the correct format out of the error text. This is one of the model's reactions to failure: fix the parameters and retry.

events.label: Execute #2
events.detail: Validation passes; the query actually runs.

events.label: tool_use #3: write the ledger
events.detail: {"id":"toolu_w1","name":"write_ledger","input":{"entries":37}}. Query done, the model requests the next action.

events.label: 429 Too Many Requests
events.detail: The ledger system rate-limits: HTTP 429 with retry-after: 1. Rate limiting, like timeouts, is the norm in engineering rather than the exception.

events.label: Exponential backoff: 1s → 2s → 4s
events.detail: The client-side guardrail: wait 1s and retry; another 429, wait 2s, then 4s… with a retry cap (5 in this example) to prevent an endless loop; honor the server's retry-after first when present. Backoff is "retrying politely", the cap is "not grinding forever".

events.label: Attempt 4 succeeds
events.detail: The backoff gave the ledger system breathing room; the write lands and returns ledger_id=L-2087.

events.label: Feed back both results
events.detail: The tool_results of toolu_r2 and toolu_w1 are replied together — the successful results and the whole failure-retry trail stay in context for the model to reference.

events.label: Final answer
events.detail: "Synced 37 refunds (¥21,340 total), written to ledger L-2087." The loop exits after delivery. The backoff-and-cap guardrail returns in lesson A07, The Runaway Experiment, from the angle of keeping loops from running away.
